requirements.location: Complete reports/current.md lines 1-270; original verifiable_self_improvement_en case and identical effective R_TASK; all language/date requirements.
requirements.basis: I read the entire full manuscript in three untruncated ranges and matched it to the original task. The report distinguishes changed weights/code/prompts/workflows from temporary adaptation; treats DGM and AlphaEvolve as different mechanisms; preserves external models, fixed outer procedures and human specifications; discusses retained artifacts, baselines, search budgets, separate future-task evidence and conditional rollback/adoption. It supplies a comparative evidence matrix, useful positive results, the limited harness-transfer result and harmful ablations. Evaluator overfitting, multiple selection, reference errors, reward exploitation, information exposure and contamination are now separate substantive analyses. The earlier outline leakage concern is therefore present in the full report without overclaiming invalidity. Program equivalence, hardware/workload conditions, deployment reports versus replication, and generation/evaluation cost boundaries are covered. One requested part of loop reconstruction remains too implicit: AlphaEvolve and Promptbreeder's actual retention/selection rules. Relevant source sections were checked directly: AlphaEvolve §§2.2-2.6 and Promptbreeder §3/figure 1 disclose more concrete behavior than appears in the manuscript. I reused prior unchanged source reading for DGM, SCoRe and HarnessPro; I did not revalidate every numerical result as a separate evidence reviewer. Current task report and frozen assignment texts match.

findings.location: Loop-classification table lines 17-23; AlphaEvolve section lines 66-82; Promptbreeder section lines 84-94; comparison matrix lines 150-157
findings.basis: R_TASK specifically asks to reconstruct each principal loop so that the selection rule and retained history can be identified. DGM has that detail, but AlphaEvolve is described only as using a seed, program database, staged rejection and performance measurement; the reader cannot tell what the database retains or how past candidates are reused to form the next proposal. Promptbreeder likewise says population selection is human-designed without stating the documented replacement rule. These are consequential to the report's search-space/feedback/transfer argument. AlphaEvolve original §§2.2 and 2.5 says programs are retained with scores and program outputs, multiple previous solutions are sampled into later prompts, and the database balances diversity/exploitation through a method inspired by MAP-Elites and island populations. Its §2.3 also identifies the Gemini 2.0 Flash/Pro generator mix. Promptbreeder official §3 describes sampling two individuals, mutating the fitter one and replacing the loser, with the unit retaining task prompts, its mutation prompt and, where used, correct worked examples. Add this disclosed candidate-to-history-to-next-generation behavior in a compact table or paragraphs. State the limits of public detail rather than inventing an exact unpublished AlphaEvolve sampling formula. No new execution is required.
